Numeric values for bias and flag constants and any batch upper bounds beyond the default.
Export visibility and allowed calling contexts for public operations beyond locking shown.

findings.text: The reference abstraction exposes operations to force atomic counting, synchronously force atomic counting until completion is visible, clear the force and restore per processor counting, mark the object dead with an optional completion callback, query whether the value is zero, and revive a dead zero object. Forcing persists until cleared. Marking dead is meant to happen once and releases the initial hold. Revival clears the dead indication and acquires a hold.

A reference is either in per processor counting or atomic counting with separate dead and forced indications. Live and unforced objects may use per processor counting while dead or forced objects use atomic counting. A set completion callback denotes a transition in flight. Exactly one completion signal per transition to atomic wakes all waiters, with a default no operation when the caller supplies none.

While per processor counting is usable the shared count carries a large positive bias that prevents concurrent activity on distinct processors from making the value look empty during folding. Returning to per processor counting restores the bias and entering atomic counting folds shard values with bias removal. A non positive shared value after folding is unexpected and triggers diagnostic reporting with limited repetition.

Mode choice plus dead marking plus force updates plus completion pointer changes are serialized by a dedicated switch lock. Public mutators take this lock with interrupts blocked. The internal decision helper asserts the lock is held and waits on a dedicated queue while completion remains pending, dropping the lock during the wait. Completion clears the pending indication and wakes all waiters. The zero query uses the same lock when sampling the shared value in atomic mode.

Repeated dead marking, revival of a live object, revival while still in per processor counting, per processor restoration without reinit permission, and reinit without observed zero are reported as programming errors through one time warnings. Missing shard storage during restoration and non positive shared value after folding are treated as fatal or warning conditions with object diagnostics.

The counter abstraction supports folding the current processor shard into the global part, exact summation across online and dying processors, grouped allocation and teardown sharing one per processor area, rough comparison against a threshold with exact fallback, and conditional addition bounded by a limit. Allocation fails cleanly on memory exhaustion. Teardown handles already released groups and nulls shard pointers after freeing.

The logical total is the global part plus all processor shards. Folding of the local shard and handling of a dying processor transfer the affected shard into the global part and reset that shard, leaving the logical total unchanged. Exact summation observes a stable snapshot with respect to concurrent folding and dying processor handling.

Each counter instance has its own raw lock protecting its global part against folding plus summation plus bounded updates plus dying processor handling. A separate global lock protects the registry of live counters. Group allocation links and group teardown unlinks under the global lock with interrupts blocked. Dying processor handling holds the global lock while taking each instance lock in turn.

The per processor batch threshold defaults to thirty two and tracks online processor count as the larger of thirty two and twice that count. Comparison trusts a cheap read when it differs from the threshold by more than one batch per online processor and otherwise uses exact summation. Bounded addition may complete without instance locking when the local effect stays within batch and uncertainty keeps the result on the allowed side, otherwise it decides precisely under lock and on success folds the local contribution.

With debug support each allocated counter is activated as a debug object under this facility name and each destroyed counter is deactivated and freed, with a fixup that destroys a still active counter. Without debug support activation is inert. With hotplug support allocation joins a global registry and teardown leaves it. Startup registers online and dead handlers for batch maintenance and shard folding and warns on registration failure.

The priority ordered list supports insertion preserving ascending priority, removal with representative upkeep, and requeue of an interior member to the end of its equal priority group. Insertion locates its position by scanning inward from both ends of the representative chain. Removal promotes a same priority successor when the removed member was its group representative. Requeue does nothing for the final member or when priority differs from the successor.

Each head maintains a complete chain of all members in priority order plus a representative chain containing the first member of each distinct priority in the same order. Non representative members keep an empty representative linkage. Removal reinitializes both linkages of the removed member. Requeue preserves group membership and the single representative per priority property.

Insertion expects a detached member with detached representative linkage. Requeue expects a non empty head and an already queued member. Debug configurations verify bidirectional linkage consistency around each mutation while the alternate configuration compiles verification away. Violations produce warnings or fatal assertions.

The viewed reference state includes a combined pointer word holding atomic and dead flag bits together with either shard location or embedded small count, a pointer to auxiliary data, and inside that data a back pointer to the owner plus callback head for deferred work plus one shot completion callback plus forced and reinit permission flags plus shared count plus release callback used in diagnostics.

The viewed counter state includes a raw lock plus signed global part plus per processor shard pointer plus, under hotplug configurations, a registry linkage. Group allocation carves one contiguous per processor area into aligned slices, one slice per group member, and initializes lock plus global part plus slice plus registry linkage per member.

The viewed list state includes a head with a full member chain and a node with integer priority plus full chain linkage plus representative linkage. Head helpers expose emptiness plus first plus next plus last plus iteration. Test scaffolding uses one head and a fixed array of two hundred forty one nodes.
The default per processor batch threshold for this counter facility is thirty two.

A built in arithmetic check validates agreement between native scalars and per processor scalars across signed and unsigned widths, exercising increment, decrement, addition, subtraction, write, read, and value returning updates around zero, negative one, all bits set, and thirty two bit wrap boundaries. Mismatches warn. Execution blocks preemption, logs start and finish, requests unload through an error return, while the exit handler is inert.

A built in ordering check validates the priority list through randomized insertion, removal, and requeue over a fixed pool, confirming member count, ascending order, and representative linkage after each mutation, then drains the structure and separately times ascending insertion to report cost.
The viewed error injection fragment declares a file local integer control for priority with no further behavior visible in range.
